Tatarbunary Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tatarbunary, Ukraine

Demolished. Existing no later than the mid-19th century per an 1860 Russian topographic map, this cemetery's remaining tombstones were reportedly removed by local authorities only recently and relocated to a gas station on Papanina Street, after decades of earlier informal demolition; a tombstone belonging to Tsirlya Padva, bearing a long poetic epitaph, lay near the Holocaust memorial three years before this survey but has since disappeared. Little is documented about the Jewish community itself, though the cemetery's 1860s existence suggests an active community by then; population reached 999 by 1897 and 1,202 by 1930. Local Jews were detained in a camp in late July 1941, and 451 were murdered on August 9, 1941.
